szoveg_eredeti:
Excited to share that today Google DeepMind and Mencap are launching Easy Read Co-Creator - a new AI tool designed to make info accessible for people with a learning disability.

(And since tech press releases aren’t always the easiest read, we ran today’s announcement through the tool itself - swipe through below to see it in action! 👇)

For 1.5M+ people in the UK with a learning disability, reading the dense yet critically important daily documents we all encounter - can be a huge barrier to everyday independence. Whether it’s hospital appointment letters, bank forms, or travel updates – Easy Read helps solve this by pairing short, simple sentences with clear images. Manually creating a single document like this used to take days or even weeks. The Co-Creator is able to do it in minutes - while keeping a human editor firmly in the lead to check, edit, & sign off every page.

And what makes me most proud is how Easy Read was built, because it’s a brilliant example of what happens when the people closest to a challenge lead the solution. It started with Dr. Alexander Cowen-Rivers at Google DeepMind & his sister Sarah Cowen-Rivers at Mencap, after a conversation with their brother Danny, who has a learning disability. It was then co-designed alongside Mencap colleagues with lived experience.

To really help to scale this - across hospitals, charities, and public services - Google.org is also providing a $1M grant to Mencap to train and onboard 50+ organizations over the next phase of the rollout. We want accessibility to be the norm, not the exception. So if your organisation wants to get involved, check out the link in the comments.
